_comment: Secondary-condition suggestion map. Each entry: primary condition pattern → plausible secondaries with the medical rationale to DISCUSS WITH A PROVIDER. These are recognized claim patterns, not medical advice; every suggestion requires a real nexus opinion (38 CFR §3.310). The analysis endpoint matches primaries by keyword and returns these with the rationale.

secondaries.rationale: Peer-reviewed literature links PTSD with higher OSA prevalence (sleep fragmentation, arousal threshold changes, medication-related weight gain). Requires sleep study + nexus opinion.
Chronic stress response and psychiatric medications (SSRIs, others) are associated with reflux; nexus opinion should address causation or aggravation.
Chronic hyperarousal and sympathetic activation are associated with elevated blood pressure; literature-supported secondary/aggravation theory.
Common side effect of SSRIs/SNRIs and of PTSD itself; typically compensated via SMC-K even at 0%.
Headache disorders frequently co-occur with and are aggravated by PTSD and sleep deprivation.
Gut-brain axis: functional GI disorders are strongly associated with chronic anxiety/PTSD.
Nerve-root compression from spine pathology radiating into limbs — rated separately per extremity under DC 8520/8510-series; check for the bilateral factor.
Chronic-pain-to-depression secondary service connection is a well-recognized pathway with strong literature support.
Antalgic gait and compensatory mechanics can cause or aggravate ipsilateral/contralateral joint pathology; nexus should address biomechanics.
Long-term NSAID therapy for service-connected pain causing/aggravating reflux or gastritis — medication-bridge secondary theory.
Pain-disrupted sleep may support a mental-health or sleep-disorder secondary; document with a sleep log.
secondaries.dbq: Mental Disorders or Sleep Apnea DBQ

secondaries.rationale: Lumbar radiculopathy and chronic opioid/pain-medication use are associated with ED (SMC-K).

Headaches originating from a service-connected CERVICAL/neck condition (cervicogenic headache) are a recognized secondary, rated on the migraine schedule (DC 8100). Most relevant when the primary is a neck condition.

Favoring an injured limb shifts load to the other side; nexus must address gait mechanics, ideally with gait analysis or provider observation. If granted, both sides trigger the bilateral factor (§4.26).
Chronic limp altering spinal mechanics is a recognized secondary path to lumbar pathology.
Chronic musculoskeletal pain is a leading driver of secondary depression claims.
Classic diabetic complication; rated per nerve per extremity — bilateral factor applies when both sides affected.
Microvascular complication; needs eye exam.
Microvascular complication; labs (eGFR, albuminuria) document it.
Vascular/neurologic complication of diabetes (SMC-K).

VA generally does NOT treat essential hypertension as a direct complication of diabetes (M21-1) — especially where the hypertension pre-dated the diabetes. The winnable theories are hypertension secondary to diabetic NEPHROPATHY (the kidney bridge) or AGGRAVATION of pre-existing hypertension; frame the nexus on one of those, not on diabetes 'causing' the hypertension.
Severe chronic tinnitus is associated with sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression; document functional impact.
Tinnitus/hearing disorders co-occur with headache disorders; weaker path — needs a solid provider opinion.
Chronic headache disorders and TBI are strongly associated with mood disorders.
TBI and chronic migraines disrupt sleep architecture.
Tinnitus is among the most common TBI residuals.
Untreated OSA is a well-established cause of secondary hypertension.
OSA's cardiovascular sequelae are literature-supported.
Chronic sleep fragmentation drives mood and cognitive symptoms.
Reflux-associated aspiration can aggravate airway disease.
Progression of untreated GERD; usually rated within the esophageal codes rather than separately — ask the provider to document severity.
Hypertensive nephropathy; labs document it.
Long-standing hypertension causing cardiac disease.
Hypertension is the dominant stroke risk factor; residuals rate under the affected functions.

Chronic nasal-airway obstruction (rhinitis, sinusitis, septal deviation, turbinate hypertrophy) impairs upper-airway patency and can cause or aggravate OSA — one of the most-recommended OSA secondaries. Requires a sleep study + nexus opinion.

Prostatectomy, radiation, or the prostate condition itself commonly causes ED — one of the most frequent ED secondaries, with near-automatic Special Monthly Compensation (SMC-K) even at a 0% ED rating.
Flat feet alter arch mechanics and load — a recognized cause of secondary plantar fasciitis (DC 5269).
Flatfoot changes gait and lower-limb alignment, which can cause or aggravate knee, hip, and low-back pathology up the kinetic chain; nexus should address biomechanics.
